thread:
jordan: FYI opened a PR to pin provider versions and refactor module sources. Want a quick sanity check before I merge. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/234

alex: Link doesn't show in the thread preview for me, pasting: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/234 — what's the exact change for module sources? switching to tags?

jordan: Yup, switching module refs from branches to explicit git tags and adding tighter provider constraints. Example in root module: `required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "~> 4.60" } }` and modules now use `source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git?ref=v1.2.0"`

maria: Did you regenerate the .terraform.lock.hcl? CI was failing for me earlier because mac darwin checksums differ from linux.

jordan: Yep, updated lockfile. Ran: ``terraform providers lock -platform=darwin_arm64 -platform=linux_amd64`` and committed the resulting `.terraform.lock.hcl`. CI run shows `terraform init`/`validate` passing on linux. Diff is small (provider checksums added for both platforms).

sam: Quick question — will pinning the provider force upgrades in production workspaces? We have a couple of older provider versions in the dedicated workspace state.

jordan: Good catch. Plan is: merge PR -> run `terraform plan` in staging workspace using the new lockfile and provider constraints. This should not change resources unless provider behavior changed. If anything looks risky we'll do a canary apply to a non-critical infra first. We won't run `terraform apply` in prod without an approval from infra-oncall. If we needed to change provider references in state we'd run `terraform state replace-provider` but I don't expect that here.

liz: Are there any breaking changes in the module v1.2.0 you're pinning to? I remember a rename in network module a while back.

jordan: I checked the changelog; the only thing was an optional param rename but the module still provides the old var as a deprecated alias. No expected breakage for our current usage. I'll add a note in the PR description about that.

tf-bot: CI check: `terraform fmt` OK, `terraform validate` OK on linux_amd64, plan succeeded in staging job (no resource changes).

alex: Looks reasonable. Two requests: 1) add an entry in `infra/UPGRADES.md` with the provider pin rationale and the lockfile command you ran, and 2) ping infra-oncall before doing the staging apply so they can watch.

jordan: Will do both. I'll wait ~24h to give folks time to review, then follow the apply checklist and ping infra-oncall. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
